title: Half of Small to Medium-Sized Businesses Still Rely on Paper Records
reason: Reports an Act! survey of more than 1,100 SMB owners in which 45% of SMB operations still rely on paper records (US).

title: SMEs still tech averse, MYOB
reason: Survey of 523 accountants and bookkeepers in Australia: 41% said at least half their SME clients provide paper documents rather than electronic ones.

title: 3 in 4 SMEs still using shoebox accounting
reason: Xero study in Australia: 77.6% of small businesses still store at least some receipts and invoices in shoeboxes; sample size not stated.

title: SMEs not on board with digital trails, research finds
reason: H&R Block and Officeworks survey in Australia: only 5% of small business owners track receipts digitally all year, most keep paper just to be safe.

title: Over half of global businesses in paper jam
reason: Basware and Institute of Financial Operations study of more than 900 finance professionals: 53% of companies still scan and capture paper invoices in-house (global, older).

title: Document management roll-up: it's time to transition to digital
reason: Cites a Software Advice survey of 576 US information workers: about six hours a week spent searching for documents in paper-based offices (2015, modest sample).

title: Meeting the challenge of high quality data entry: a free double-entry system
reason: Academic paper arguing small businesses rely on minimally trained staff for manual data entry and proposing a free double-entry verification method; no figures given.

title: Streamlining data recording through optical character recognition: a prospective multi-center study in intensive care units
reason: Multi-center ICU study in 3 countries: OCR-based entry reached 96.9% accuracy and took 3.4 minutes per patient versus 6.0 manual, over 1,018 validated data points (hospital setting, not small firms).

title: SMEs spend up to 1000 a year on paper: why Telstra says your business needs to up your apps
reason: Reports a Telstra survey of 1,000 Australian small business owners: SMEs spend up to $1,000 a year on paper (vendor-commissioned, 2014).

title: Why Handwritten Forms Still Break Smart AI
reason: Benchmark run by a vendor CEO (not peer reviewed): even the best AI models struggled to consistently exceed 95% business-level accuracy on real handwritten forms.

title: Aguilar, Lind and Ramesh: accounting records in informal microbusinesses (working paper)
reason: ILO survey of about 1,400 firms in Guatemala, Honduras and El Salvador: 44% of informal microbusinesses keep systematic records, about three-quarters of them on notebooks (PDF unreadable in fetch; figures from search summary, to verify).
